title: SQ-triggered Pricing Escalation & Cost-Recovery Matrix
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Problem: Sales and Solutions Engineering receive security questionnaire (SQ) requests that vary widely in scope. Current handling is ad-hoc: discounts or additional SOWs are negotiated without consistent cost recovery or approval guardrails, creating revenue leakage and legal/risk exposure.

Goal: Design and roll out an operational matrix that 1) classifies SQs by complexity/effort, 2) maps each complexity tier to required approvals, default pricing adjustments (discount caps, surcharge or SOW recommendation), and 3) updates the pricebook and quoting templates so sellers consistently capture compliance effort. This should reduce manual approvals, speed time-to-quote, and ensure cost recovery for heavy SQ work.
acceptance_criteria: A classification rubric (Tier 0-3) for SQ complexity with example questions and estimated engineering/legal hours per tier
An approval matrix that ties Tier -> required approver(s) (AE quota level, Sales Manager, Legal, PM) and auto-escalation rules
Pricebook entries for: standard discount caps per tier, optional one-time compliance surcharge SKUs, and SOW recommendation text
Updated quoting workflow (Salesforce/CPQ or manual template) with a checkbox for SQ-tier that pre-populates pricing adjustments
Confluence PRD and Google Sheet cost model reviewed and signed off by Legal and Finance
Two pilot quotes executed (one mid-market, one enterprise) using the matrix and retro review completed

decision_log: 2025-01-20: Decided to use a 4-tier rubric (0=basic, 3=extensive) rather than 3 tiers to capture high-effort outliers (approved by Lina & Ethan)
2025-01-28: Finance recommended a one-time compliance surcharge rather than raising recurring fees; approved for pilot to keep revenue clean
2025-02-05: Legal required an opt-out clause for customers that will sign an explicit SOW; agreed and added SOW templates
2025-02-12: Sales Ops pushed back on too many approval steps for mid-market; settled on auto-approve for Tier 0-1 under AE quota threshold
comments: 2025-01-19 - Maya Thompson (Solutions Eng): Initial rubric draft attached in Drive; estimate Tier 3 = 40+ hrs legal/engineering; request examples from Support.
2025-01-22 - Raj Patel (Finance): Ran cost-recovery sensitivity. If surcharge set too low we still lose >10% margin on complex deals. Recommend $5k-$20k one-time bands.
2025-02-02 - Ana Ruiz (Legal): Reviewed draft SOW language; need clarity on data handling clauses for regulated customers; see Confluence comment link.
2025-02-11 - Jordan Lee (Sales): Pilot AE says checkbox increased quote time by 2 minutes but prevented 2 retroactive discount requests — positive signal.
2025-02-18 - Lina Gomez (PM): Incorporated Sales Ops feedback; lowered approval friction for Tier 1; prepping rollout comms for next week.
notes: We want to avoid creating an approval bottleneck for self-serve or low-touch mid-market deals. Pilot must measure: time-to-quote delta, % of deals with surcharge applied, and post-sale effort hours. If pilot shows >15% seller friction, we will iterate by shifting to post-signature SOW charge workflow.
